rounds.fact: Charles Schwab was one of the first traditional brokerages to fully embrace online trading, helping legitimize the idea for investors who didn't trust newer online-only upstarts.
Photobucket became the default way millions of MySpace users hosted images for their profiles, since MySpace itself didn't offer easy photo uploading in its early years.
Edmunds built its reputation on detailed car reviews and true-cost-to-own data, becoming a trusted resource for buyers trying to negotiate against dealerships.
Juno offered free dial-up internet paid for entirely by advertising, and later merged with rival NetZero to survive the end of the free-ISP era.
Newegg built a loyal following among PC builders by focusing almost entirely on computer parts, with a reputation for detailed listings and fast shipping that rivaled Amazon in that niche.
